Senses.Explanation: The sameness-half of the paired formula — the clouds and moon the same though streams and mountains differ — ruled at the Luopu visit and turned across eight centuries of halls. The root sits in Jiashan Shanhui's own ruling, carried in Xuedou Chongxian's case-raising: Luopu, long Linji's attendant, comes from afar begging one receiving — no monk before me, no old monk here — Luopu shouts, and Jiashan stops him: hold, hold, no hurrying — the clouds and moon are the same, streams and mountains differ; cutting off every tongue under heaven, not denied — but how will you get the tongueless man to speak? — and at Luopu's silence, the blow that seated him at Jiashan's side for years; Xuedou's own comment, carried in Gulin Qingmao's re-raising, pities the man for dulling Linji — since he is clouds-and-moon-the-same, I am streams-and-mountains-differing — what talk of tongueless speaking, and the sitting-cloth snapped in his face: had Jiashan been a man who knows the directions, he would have set it under the bright window; Huanxi Weiyi, arriving at Ruiyan where the nation's-first ancestor's eyebrows are knotted into the hills, turns the pair twice — streams and mountains differ, the clouds and moon are the same; since the clouds and moon are the same, what talk of streams and mountains differing? — until carriages and script run as one, one man sits high doing nothing, all lands return to the utmost turning; and Wuyi Yuanlai, opening the retreat against the same-root saying, answers it with a letter — yesterday someone came from Yanjing bearing a letter from Guangnan: have you not seen the streams and mountains differ while the clouds and moon are the same? Yongjue Yuanxian, on his birthday, lifts the fan: this — opened, each differs from each, streams and mountains apart; shut, the ten directions cut off, the clouds and moon one — and as for neither opening nor shutting? today the three-era buddhas shed light and shake the earth atop this old monk's fan; Tian'an Sheng, at the Qingzhou hall, spreads it to the compass — heaven covering all, every house clouds-and-moon-the-same, north and south one road whose ruts join; earth bearing all, every border unblocked, Qi and Lu one wind without reforming — yet this, he rules, is still corner-keeping, unfit to continue the gate: to catch the rootless tree upside down and haul the Haituo's old wind-rules, heaven's gate must be swung and the earth's axis overturned; Baiyu Jingsi turns the pair against its knowers — dung-beetles and grubs sporting the thirty-two marks, sands and thorns shedding the hundred thousand rays, sage and commoner one body without gap — and yet, fine as that is, thirty blows at the heel: for knowing only the clouds-and-moon-the-same, who recognizes the streams and mountains differing?; and Jifei Ruyi, in the lineage ode for the thirtieth heir Tianqi Benrui, gives the formula the succession itself — clouds and moon the same, one plain sweep of the ancient emperor's wind; the buddhas do not know him, and he outfaces buddha and patriarch; the seeing and hearing of before were never seeing and hearing — one branch of the udumbara red, alone bared.
